summary: Add provider-neutral, tenant-scoped OIDC configuration with deployment-owned URL allowlists, SecretProvider-backed client secrets, validation-before-activation and immutable rollback evidence through the existing Keycloak/enterprise-IAM boundary.

impacts.evidence: Provider heads, immutable revisions and validation evidence are organization/workspace scoped and protected by forced RLS.
Client secret plaintext is accepted once through SecretProvider and excluded from revisions, responses, audit and validation evidence.
OpenAPI 0.13.0 adds six authenticated settings operations and regenerated SDK methods without changing existing operations.
No EventBus schema or canonical envelope changes.
Connector and plugin SDK contracts are unchanged; provider_id is configuration rather than connector dispatch.
Expand migration 000065 adds three tenant-scoped settings tables with immutable revision and validation evidence.

Issuer and metadata URLs require HTTPS, an exact deployment allowlist, public DNS answers, pinned dialing, bounded responses and no redirects; activation requires successful current-revision evidence.
All mutations require the admin-only settings.identity_providers.write capability and are classified write_sensitive.
Draft, validation, activation, disable and rollback operations append actor/correlation evidence without secret values.
Optimistic versions and persisted correlation identifiers make management command retries replay-safe; rollback creates a new monotonic revision.
OIDC discovery is the only new egress and is constrained by the deployment allowlist and SSRF-safe pinned transport.
The UI exposes draft, validation and active revision states without claiming provider health beyond discovery validation.
The additive migration preserves old readers; application rollback copies an already validated historical revision instead of rewriting evidence.
URL policy, secret non-disclosure, validation failure, migration invariants, OpenAPI parity, generated SDK and frontend checks cover the change.
